study type: Retrospective cohort study with propensity score matching
exposure: Subxiphoid single-port robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (SRATS) thymectomy using the single-port robotic system (SPS)
Subxiphoid single-port video-assisted thoracic surgery (SVATS) thymectomy
cohort: The cohort consisted of 110 patients who underwent subxiphoid SRATS and SVATS thymectomy at three institutions between September 2018 and May 2024, with 50 patients (25 per group) included after propensity score matching.
finding: Subxiphoid SRATS thymectomy was associated with a lower conversion rate to multi-port surgery, shorter chest tube drainage duration, and a shorter postoperative hospital stay compared to SVATS thymectomy.
